comparison_with_the_scan.reading: the angle between the two fitted axes equals the sum of the two published angles within 0.02 degrees. Each axis is about 0.4 degrees from its published angle, in opposite directions, which is the size of the difference the twin already found between its two ways of building a valve axis. The fitted guide bore is half a millimetre smaller than the production stem: this head does not take the production 9 mm valve, which agrees with the 8 mm stems in the maker's catalogue (docs/research/935-faithful-replica-20261028/README.md)
comparison_with_the_scan.what_it_does_not_show: the form describes another head. The agreement does not calibrate the scan, and it does not identify the inlet: it is one more indication that valve_y_minus is the inlet, beside the larger seat. H09 stays open until a specification or a marked photograph of the specimen says so

fatigue.question: published fatigue data of laser powder bed fusion AlSi10Mg, above all at temperature
fatigue.standing: published values, read as stated below. None is admitted as material data: the repository admits no fatigue data (docs/AGENT_TOOL_GUIDE.md), and admitting any of these is a decision this record does not take

sets.authors_reading: no clear improvement of the fatigue performance after the two heat treatments

conditions.heat_treatment: not found in the passages read

result.conditions: fully reversed, turned, no heat treatment, temperature not stated

sets.note: already held in the catalogue; listed because it sits 50 MPa above the previous set for the same loading

conditions.treatment: hot isostatic pressing at 515 °C, 100 MPa, 3 h; then aged in air at 177 °C; machined after ageing
conditions.stress_level_is: not defined as a maximum or an amplitude

sets.note: one unaged Z specimen passed 5 million cycles and is left out of its mean by the authors; at the lower level (62 MPa) every specimen passed 5 million

sets.main_session: conditions re-read in the text; the table values not re-read

conditions.treatment: stress relief at 285 °C for 120 min, or hot isostatic pressing and T6; then aged at 177 °C for 0, 10, 100 or 1000 h
conditions.stress_level_is: not defined as a maximum or an amplitude

result.stress_relieved_at_124_MPa: 20 of 24 specimens ran out, at every ageing time
result.hip_t6_at_145_MPa: every specimen ran out up to 100 h of ageing; at 1000 h the mean life is 182,952 (XY) and 61,364 (Z)

conditions.treatments: T5 (4 h at 160 °C); rapid T6 (10 min at 510 °C, then 6 h at 160 °C)

result.exposure: up to 17 h at 200 °C brings no macroscopic change of the microstructure

conditions.material: cast A356 with 0.5% copper, T7, cut from the valve bridges of cylinder heads: not a printed alloy
conditions.loading: strain controlled, ASTM E606, strain ratio −1

not_found: a stress-controlled S-N curve at 100 to 300 °C with its points, in a document that could be opened: the two values at 200 °C and the one at 350 °C are single strengths from abstracts
a test that combines a long soak with testing at temperature: the 177 °C ageing sets were tested at room temperature
as-built surfaces at temperature, thermo-mechanical fatigue, or the effect of mean stress at temperature
a review with a table of points that could be opened; a public database of 1,610 S-N sets exists (doi 10.1038/s41597-023-02150-x) and was not opened
contradictions: fully reversed strength of machined coupons: 110 MPa at 2e7 cycles on the machine maker's sheet, 60 MPa at 1e7 in the Kramer set
T6: reported to help in three papers and to reduce life in a fourth, as quoted by a review
stress relief: no gain in the Roveda set, where the run-out range falls from 130 to 120 to 100 MPa
surface: one group finds ground and as-built surfaces alike, another finds machining clearly better
exposure: 'no variation' after 17 h at 200 °C, against lives falling by a factor of 60 or more after 1000 h at 177 °C

port-flow.question: published flow-bench data of these heads, and the references needed to compare a computed port flow with a bench

values.quantity: inlet opening of the head at the manifold face, height x width
values.note: the height includes the injector notch

values.quantity: opening of the inlet manifold at the head, height x width
smallest diameter of the inlet pipe, 930 Turbo 3.0

method_references.what: definition of the flow coefficient: mass flow = nominal valve area · C · sqrt(2 · density · pressure drop), with the nominal area (π/4) D² of the valve
method_references.note: D is the smallest contact diameter of valve and seat (not re-read); test at a pressure drop of 10 in. of alcohol

method_references.what: cycle-mean flow coefficient 0.445 at a lift of a quarter of the valve diameter, for two valve sizes
peak flow coefficient about 0.68 at lift / diameter 0.25 and about 0.60 at 0.198
computed against measured, helical diesel port, 523,000 cells: the global discharge coefficient is about 6% under the measurement
computed against measured, four-valve petrol head, 99,500 cells at 5.0 kPa: largest discrepancy 8%
bench practice: test pressures of 10, 25 or 28 in. of water are all in use; one practitioner chose 28 in. after finding little change of the port balance below 26 in.

derived_here.quantity: factor between flows at two test pressures, if flow goes as the square root of the pressure drop: 10 to 28, 25 to 28, 10 to 25 in. of water
derived_here.note: follows from the orifice equation above; a bench maker's note warns that it is not exact at high velocity
